root.claim: There is one deterministic Turing machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes that, for every $n\ge1$, outputs $\operatorname{bin}_{2n}(\operatorname{val}(x)\operatorname{val}(y))$ on input $x\#y$ with $x,y\in\{0,1\}^n$ in worst-case time $T_A(n)=O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$, $\kappa=2^{-182}$, which disproves the Schönhage–Strassen $n\log n$ optimality conjecture in this model.
root.method: Build two tape procedures that beat one pass per level by a power, an address-chunk interchange and a simultaneous butterfly layer, from fixed linear networks with a rank saving; use them to evaluate the Harvey–van der Hoeven reduction of the digit convolution to power-of-two synthetic transforms; and bound every cost divided by $V=Tp$ by the power $p^{1-2\kappa}$.

motivation.text: In the O(n log n) approach every one of the Θ(log n) transform levels scans all Θ(n) stored bits, so going below n log n needs cheaper data movement and cheaper butterfly arithmetic per level, which the two tape procedures supply.

quote.quote: Scanning an array of $\Theta(n)$ stored bits at each of $\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$. We therefore need savings in both movement and arithmetic.

adds.name: input length
adds.meaning: The number of bits of each of the two input integers.

adds.name: saving exponent
adds.meaning: The fixed exponent $\kappa=2^{-182}$ by which the logarithmic factor is reduced, half of the smallest cost margin.

root.salient: The improvement is a strict power of the logarithm, $(\lg n)^{-\kappa}$ with a tiny but fixed $\kappa=2^{-182}$, and it traces back to one strict integer inequality $s<Wm$ in a fixed finite network.

children.claim: The time bound refutes the $n\log n$ optimality conjecture of Schönhage and Strassen in the fixed-tape model: an eventual lower bound would need constants $c_A>0$ and $N_A$ with $T_A(n)\ge c_An\lg n$ for all $n\ge N_A$, whereas here $T_A(n)/(n\lg n)\to0$.
children.method: Unfold what an eventual lower bound for every fixed machine means and negate it with one machine.

motivation.text: The conjecture is a claim about every fixed machine, so a single machine whose cost divided by $n\lg n$ tends to zero refutes it.

children.claim: In the fixed-tape model, an eventual $n\log n$ lower bound means that for each fixed machine $A$ there are constants $c_A>0$ and $N_A$ with $T_A(n)\ge c_An\lg n$ whenever $n\ge N_A$.

quote.quote: an eventual lower bound for every multiplication machine means that, for each fixed machine $A$, there are constants $c_A>0$ and $N_A$ such that $T_A(n)\ge c_A n\lg n$ whenever $n\ge N_A$.

children.claim: Its negation needs one machine with $\liminf_{n\to\infty}T_A(n)/(n\lg n)=0$, and the bound $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ gives the stronger $\lim_{n\to\infty}T_A(n)/(n\lg n)=0$ through all input lengths.

quote.quote: The power saving proved here gives a limit of zero through all input lengths, which is a stronger conclusion.

children.claim: Two tape procedures save a power over one pass per parameter unit: interchanging two disjoint contiguous $u$-bit address fields of an array of stored volume $V$ costs $O(Vu^\tau)$, and a simultaneous normalized butterfly $H_0$ on one selected bit of each of $D\le d$ address chunks costs $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$, with $\tau=1-2^{-50}$ and $\lambda'=1-2^{-54}$.
children.method: Construct a fixed linear network, in a bit and a complex variant, that exchanges two banks while restoring arbitrary scratch values, label its vertices with nested subspaces so that the total edge rank $s$ is below $Wm$, and run it on $W$ row-split role streams of volume $V/W$ so that each unit of edge rank becomes one recursive call at the parameter divided by $m$.

motivation.text: Each unit of edge rank is one recursive call on a stream of $1/W$ of the volume, so per unit volume a factor $m$ in the parameter costs a factor $s/W$; when $s<Wm$ this is below $m$, and unrolling gives a cost growing like a power below one of the parameter.

quote.quote: After dividing cost by volume, multiplying the parameter by $m$ increases the recursive contribution by $s/W<m$. This strict inequality is the source of the power saving.

adds.name: logical volume
adds.meaning: The number of stored data bits of the array being processed, excluding work tapes and duplicate streams.

adds.name: wire count
adds.meaning: The number of wires, or roles, of the fixed network: $W_{\rm b}$ for the bit variant and $W_{\rm c}$ for the complex variant.

adds.name: label dimension
adds.meaning: The dimension $m=h^3=10^6$ of the label space, which is also the factor by which the parameter shrinks per recursion level.

adds.name: total edge rank
adds.meaning: The sum over all network edges of the rank of the frame change, which is the number of recursive calls one node makes: $s_{\rm b}$ or $s_{\rm c}$.

adds.name: interchange exponent
adds.meaning: The fixed exponent $\tau=1-2^{-50}$ in the interchange cost $O(Vu^\tau)$, with $s/W<m^\tau$.

adds.name: layer exponent
adds.meaning: The fixed exponent $\lambda'=1-2^{-54}$ in the butterfly-layer cost $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$.

children.salient: A node makes $s\approx Wm$ recursive calls, far more than the $m$ pieces its parameter splits into, yet the cost per unit volume grows by only $s/W<m^{1-2^{-50}}$ per factor $m$; and the interchange, an exact permutation, is computed through XOR combinations of the data.

children.claim: On a fixed number of tapes, elementary stream operations on an array of stored volume $V$ cost $O(V)$: fixed permutations and moves of radix-$q$ digits, split–map–merge on a digit, cyclic splitting of whole rows into $W$ streams, and controlled shifts and fixed rational scalings of a target field that follows its controls.
children.method: Split the stream into a fixed number of aligned sub-streams determined by the specified digits or offsets, process them, and merge them back, with counters whose total cost is linear.

motivation.text: These linear operations are the base cases and the per-node overhead of both recursive tape procedures, so each must cost only a constant number of passes over the data.

children.claim: An array on $[a_1]\times\cdots\times[a_t]$ is stored in lexicographic order with implicit addresses, and for a fixed radix $q$ each of the following costs $O(V)$: a fixed permutation of the digits at two positions, moving one digit, splitting on a digit and merging after a pointwise map, and splitting the rows of $[P]\times[R]\times[B]$ cyclically into $W$ streams of volume $V/W$, merged back when $W\mid R$.

quote.quote: Each of the following operations on an array of volume $V$ takes $O(V)$ steps on a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes

children.claim: For a fixed prime $q$ and $Q=q^b$, an update $y\mapsto y+a(\text{controls})\pmod Q$ of a target field that follows its control fields costs $O(V)$ whenever the offset is prepared in $b^{O(1)}$ time, by splitting each fiber's $Q$ blocks at $Q-a$ and merging the two pieces in swapped order; multiplying $y$ by a fixed rational unit, or its inverse, also costs $O(V)$.

quote.quote: costs $O(V)$ if the offset can be prepared in $b^{O(1)}$ time from the fixed number of control values.

children.claim: Both fixed networks, a bit network with $W_{\rm b}$ wires and a complex network with $W_{\rm c}$ wires, exchange two banks up to sign while restoring every scratch value, and admit frames whose edge changes have total rank $s_{\rm b}<W_{\rm b}m$ and $s_{\rm c}<W_{\rm c}m$, indeed $s_{\rm b}/W_{\rm b}<m^\tau$ and $s_{\rm c}/W_{\rm c}<m^\sigma$ with $\tau=\sigma=1-2^{-50}$.
children.method: Build a three-stage scalar exchange from gather, scatter, copy and side-injection gates indexed by three-element subsets of $[h]$, attach nested nondegenerate subspaces of $\mathcal F=F^{\otimes3}$ to its vertices so that dimension is lost only where a central wire returns, and turn dimension changes into edge ranks by projections (bit variant) or phase frames (complex variant).

motivation.text: With fixed source and sink labels the signed dimension changes sum to $Wm-2N$, so the total edge rank exceeds that only through dimension lost on decreasing edges; keeping that loss $L$ below $N/2$ leaves a strict deficit below $Wm$.

quote.quote: The saving will come from keeping the total dimension lost on decreasing edges small relative to $N$.

adds.name: ground-set size
adds.meaning: The size $h=100$ of the ground set $[h]$ whose three-element subsets index the banks.

adds.name: bank size
adds.meaning: The number $N=\binom{100}{3}^3=4227952113000000$ of wires in each of the two data banks.

adds.name: dimension loss
adds.meaning: The total label dimension lost along decreasing edges of the network.

children.salient: The same triple indicator vectors serve both variants through two different pairings, $|S\cap T|-1$ over $\mathbb Q$ and $|S\cap T|\bmod2$ over $\mathbb F_2$, and give nearly equal loss ratios $L/N=100/539$ and $101/539$, both below $1/2$.

children.claim: For banks $X_a,Y_a$ indexed by $a\in\mathcal T^3$, where $\mathcal T$ is the set of three-element subsets of $[h]$ with $h=100$, the eight-row schedule run forward at stage 1, inverted at stage 2 and forward at stage 3 sends $(X_a,Y_a)\mapsto(-Y_a,X_a)$ and restores every scratch wire whatever its initial value, in a bit network with $W_{\rm b}=177176569091445000000$ wires and a complex network with $W_{\rm c}=1873807244643542670000$ wires.
children.method: Show that one invocation adds $(\mathcal J\mathcal V+\mathcal R\mathcal G)x$ to its target independently of the scratch values, check from intersection sizes that this coefficient matrix is the identity in both variants, and compose the three stages.

motivation.text: Subtracting the old scratch contribution before injecting the new one, and undoing the copies afterwards, makes the result independent of whatever the scratch wires held, so existing data can later serve as scratch.

quote.quote: This cancellation of arbitrary initial scratch values is a linear instance of the restoration construction for transparent computation

adds.name: invocation count
adds.meaning: The number $I=3v^2=78440670000$ of separate invocations of the eight-row schedule over the three stages.

children.claim: With $v=\binom h3=161700$, $N=v^3=4227952113000000$ and $m=h^3=1000000$, stage $j$ fixes two coordinates of $a$ and runs $v^2$ separate invocations on the $v$ values varying in coordinate $j$, so there are $I=3v^2=78440670000$ invocations, each with its own scratch wires: a side wire $A_{ST}$ per ordered neighbor pair, central wires $C_i$ for $i\in[h]$, and $C_\ast$ in the complex variant.

quote.quote: There are two data banks $X_a,Y_a$, indexed by $a=(a_1,a_2,a_3)\in\mathcal T^3$.

children.claim: In the bit variant scalars lie in $\mathbb F_2$, $S,T$ are neighbors when $|S\cap T|=1$, copy adds $x_T$ to $A_{ST}$, side injection adds $\sum_{T:|S\cap T|=1}A_{ST}$ to $y_S$, gather adds $\sum_{T\ni i}x_T$ to $C_i$ and scatter adds $\sum_{i\in S}C_i$ to $y_S$; in the complex variant scalars lie in $\mathbb Z[i,1/2]$, neighbors are distinct triples with even intersection, side injection adds $-\sum_T\frac{|S\cap T|-1}{2}A_{ST}$, gather also adds $\sum_Tx_T$ to $C_\ast$, and scatter adds $(\sum_{i\in S}C_i-C_\ast)/2$.

quote.quote: In the bit construction, scalars lie in $\mathbb F_2$, and $S,T$ are neighbors when $|S\cap T|=1$.

children.claim: The forward schedule has eight rows: 0 subtract side injection, 1 subtract scatter, 2 copy, 3 gather, 4 scatter, 5 side injection, 6 undo gather, 7 undo copy; rows 0–1 remove the old scratch effect, rows 2–5 bring in the sources $x$ and add their effect to the targets $y$, and rows 6–7 restore the scratch.

quote.quote: The first two rows of the following schedule remove the effect of the old scratch values; the next four introduce the source values and add their effect to the target; the last two restore the scratch values.

children.claim: If the side and central scratch vectors start at $a,c$, rows 0–1 subtract $\mathcal Ja+\mathcal Rc$ from $y$, rows 2–3 change them to $a+\mathcal Vx$ and $c+\mathcal Gx$, rows 4–5 add $\mathcal R(c+\mathcal Gx)+\mathcal J(a+\mathcal Vx)$ and rows 6–7 restore $a,c$, so the target changes by $(\mathcal J\mathcal V+\mathcal R\mathcal G)x$ for every $a,c$.

quote.quote: The net target change is $(\mathcal J\mathcal V+\mathcal R\mathcal G)x$, independently of $a,c$.

children.claim: The net coefficient from $x_T$ to $y_S$ is the identity in both variants: in the bit variant the central part is $|S\cap T|\bmod2$, the side wires cancel exactly the intersection-one pairs, intersections zero and two already give zero and the self coefficient is $1$; in the complex variant the central part is $(|S\cap T|-1)/2$, the side wires cancel intersections zero and two, intersection one gives zero and the self coefficient is $(3-1)/2=1$.

quote.quote: Thus both net maps are $y\gets y+x$.

children.claim: The inverse schedule from $Y$ to $X$ effects $X\gets X-Y$, so the three stages send $(x,y)$ to $(x,y+x)$, then $(-y,y+x)$, then $(-y,x)$, which in the bit case is the permutation exchanging the banks, and each invocation restores its own scratch wires.

quote.quote: Starting from $(x,y)$, the three stages give $(x,y+x)$, then $(-y,y+x)$, then $(-y,x)$.

children.claim: A triple has $z_{\rm b}=3\binom{97}{2}=13968$ neighbors in the bit variant and $z_{\rm c}=\binom{97}{3}+3\cdot97=147731$ (intersections zero and two) in the complex variant; counting $vz$ ordered side wires and $c_{\rm b}=100$ or $c_{\rm c}=101$ central wires per invocation, $W=2N+I(vz+c)$ gives $W_{\rm b}=177176569091445000000$ and $W_{\rm c}=1873807244643542670000$.

quote.quote: Ordered pairs must be counted: there are $vz$ side wires in each invocation, not $vz/2$.

children.claim: If every wire carries an array in $R^\Omega$ with each gate applied pointwise, and every vertex $v$ has an invertible frame $D_v$, common to all incidences of a gate, with $D_vD_u^{-1}$ applied on each edge $u\to v$, then the implemented operator is $D_{\rm out}\mathsf S_\Omega D_{\rm in}^{-1}$; for a signed role permutation the route from input role $w$ to output role $\rho(w)$ applies $\varepsilon_wD_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$, on scratch roles too, whatever the intermediate frames.

quote.quote: Thus the common frame commutes with the pointwise gate, and the invariant continues to the sinks.

children.claim: Nested nondegenerate subspaces of $\mathcal F=F^{\otimes3}$, of dimension $m$, can be attached to all vertices, with source labels $U_a,0,0$ and sink labels $\mathcal F,U_a^\perp,\mathcal F$ on $X_a$, $Y_a$ and scratch roles, so that the only decreasing edges are the $Ic$ central-wire returns, each losing $h$; hence $L=Ich$, the absolute dimension changes sum to $Wm-2N+2L$, and $L_{\rm b}/N=100/539$, $L_{\rm c}/N=101/539$.
children.method: Pick a bilinear form in which neighboring triple indicators are orthogonal, prescribe stage transitions that expose one tensor factor per stage, assign common gate labels from $A\otimes F=(B\otimes F)\perp(P\otimes F)$, and tabulate the orthogonal residual of every edge.

motivation.text: The terminals fix the signed sum of dimension changes, so the only freedom is where dimension is lost; orthogonality of neighboring triples lets side wires pass through nested labels, which confines every loss to one return per central wire.

children.claim: Over $F=\mathbb Q^h$ with $\langle x,y\rangle=x^{\mathsf T}(I-J/9)y$ (eigenvalues $1$ and $-91/9$) the triple indicators satisfy $\langle t_S,t_T\rangle=|S\cap T|-1$ and $\langle t_T,t_T\rangle=2$, while over $F=\mathbb F_2^h$ with the dot product $t_T\cdot t_T=1$; in both label fields every triple line is nondegenerate and neighboring triple lines are orthogonal.

quote.quote: Thus every triple line is nondegenerate, and neighboring triple lines are orthogonal, in the label field belonging to either construction.

children.claim: With $u_a=t_{a_1}\otimes t_{a_2}\otimes t_{a_3}$ and $U_a=\langle u_a\rangle$, source dimensions sum to $N$ and sink dimensions to $Wm-N$, and each gate's incoming and outgoing labels agree, so the signed dimension changes sum to $Wm-2N$ and the absolute ones to $Wm-2N+2L$.

quote.quote: Thus the signed dimension changes will sum to $Wm-2N$, because the contributions at gates cancel.

children.claim: At stage $j$, with $A=F^{\otimes(j-1)}$, $P=\langle t_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_{j-1}}\rangle$, $B=P^\perp\subset A$ and $Q$ the line of the later factors, an $X$ wire goes from $A\otimes\langle t\rangle\otimes Q$ to $(A\otimes F)\otimes Q$ and a $Y$ wire from $B\otimes\langle t\rangle\otimes Q$ to $((B\otimes F)\perp(P\otimes t^\perp))\otimes Q$, which are exactly the next stage's incoming labels, starting at $U_a,0$ and ending at $\mathcal F,U_a^\perp$.

quote.quote: These transitions expose one tensor factor at each stage.

children.claim: Gates touch the physical wires in the order $Y$-side, $Y$-center, $X$-side, $X$-center, $Y$-center, $Y$-side, $X$-center, $X$-side at times $0,\dots,7$ with common labels $B\otimes\langle t\rangle$, $B\otimes F$, $(B\otimes F)\perp(P\otimes\langle t\rangle)$, $A\otimes F$, $B\otimes F$, $(B\otimes F)\perp(P\otimes t^\perp)$, $A\otimes F$, $A\otimes F$ (tensored by $Q$), so a side wire passes $P\otimes\langle t_X\rangle\subset P\otimes t_Y^\perp\subset P\otimes F$ and a central wire returns once from $A\otimes F$ to $B\otimes F$.

quote.quote: A central wire returns once from the former label to the latter, losing exactly $P\otimes F$.

children.claim: Every edge joins comparable labels, and with $a=h^{j-1}$, $f=h^{3-j}$ the residual dimensions are, on $X$: $\mathrm{in}\to2$ $(a-1)(h-1)$, $2\to3$ $h-1$, $3\to6$ and $6\to7$ zero; on $Y$: $\mathrm{in}\to0$ zero, $0\to1$ $(a-1)(h-1)$, $1\to4$ zero, $4\to5$ $h-1$; on a central wire: source$\to1$ $(a-1)h$, then $1\to3$, $3\to4$, $4\to6$ $h$ each; on a side wire: source$\to0$ $a-1$, $0\to2$ $(a-1)(h-1)+1$, $2\to5$ $h-2$ (using $t_X\perp t_Y$), $5\to7$ one; on scratch last$\to$sink $ah(f-1)$; only the central $3\to4$ edges decrease, so $L=Ich$.

quote.quote: Label dimension is nondecreasing along every edge except center $3\to4$, which removes $P\otimes F\otimes Q$.

children.claim: Over $\mathbb F_2$ every nonzero residual contains a norm-one vector built from coordinate units outside small supports, so it is nondegenerate and nonalternating and has an orthonormal basis, obtained by splitting off unit lines and absorbing each alternating plane $a,b$ into a unit vector $w$ through $w+a$, $w+b$, $w+a+b$.

quote.quote: Thus every nonzero residual is nonalternating.

children.claim: With $c_{\rm b}=100$ and $c_{\rm c}=101$ central wires per invocation, $L_{\rm b}/N=100/539$ and $L_{\rm c}/N=101/539$, both smaller than $1/2$.

quote.quote: In particular, both are smaller than $1/2$.

children.claim: Assigning the projection $P_U$ onto the label $U$ along $U^\perp$ to every gate and sink, $-P_{U_a}$ to the source of $X_a$ and $0$ to every other source, the bit network satisfies $M_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}-M_{\mathrm{source}(w)}=I_m$ for every role and has total edge rank $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}m-N+2L_{\rm b}=177176569088785861287000000<W_{\rm b}m$.
children.method: Identify each edge's rational rank with its label dimension change, correct for the negative source projections, and evaluate the endpoint differences.

motivation.text: With frames given by address shears $\Phi_{M_v}$, an endpoint difference $I_m$ makes the network apply the same shear $H\gets H+D$ to every role, and each edge then needs one smaller interchange per unit of its rational rank.

quote.quote: The following identity makes it the same shear $H\gets H+D$ on every role

children.claim: For a matrix $M$ the frame $\Phi_M$ moves the array entry at $(H,D)$ to $(H+MD,D)$ over a radix coprime to the denominators; it is an invertible permutation with $\Phi_{M'}\Phi_M=\Phi_{M'+M}$, so in the frame identity each routed role undergoes exactly the shear by its endpoint matrix difference.

quote.quote: Using $D_v=\Phi_{M_v}$ in \eqref{eq:common-frame-identity}, the endpoint matrix difference on each routed role is exactly the shear applied to that role.

children.claim: For nondegenerate $U\subset V$, $P_V-P_U$ is the identity on $V\cap U^\perp$ and zero on its orthogonal complement, so its rational rank is $\dim V-\dim U$, and reversing an edge negates the matrix without changing its rank.

quote.quote: Its rank is $\dim V-\dim U$; reversing the edge negates the matrix without changing its rank.

children.claim: The only exceptions are the $N$ negative source projections: at stage 1 $B=0$ and the first gate on $X_a$ has label $U_a$, so that edge matrix is $2P_{U_a}$, of rank one where the dimension change was zero, giving $s_{\rm b}=(W_{\rm b}m-2N+2L_{\rm b})+N$ with deficit $N-2L_{\rm b}>0$.

quote.quote: Its first edge matrix is therefore $2P_{U_a}$, of rational rank one, where the corresponding dimension change was zero.

children.claim: For input $X_a$ the endpoint difference is $P_{U_a^\perp}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m$, and every other role has zero source matrix and identity sink matrix.

quote.quote: For an input $X_a$ the endpoint difference is $P_{U_a^\perp}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m$.

children.claim: With $q_U(x)=\operatorname{wt}(P_Ux)\bmod4$ and frames $\mathcal C_U=H^{\otimes m}\operatorname{diag}_x(i^{q_U(x)})H^{\otimes m}$ on functions of $x\in\mathbb F_2^m$, every edge change $\mathcal C_V\mathcal C_U^{-1}$ of the complex network is a product of one translation kernel $aI+bX_v$ or its inverse per vector of an orthonormal residual basis, there are $s_{\rm c}=W_{\rm c}m-2N+2L_{\rm c}=1873807244636671267308000000<W_{\rm c}m$ such kernels, and after diagonal source and sink corrections and undoing the signed exchange the network applies $C^{\otimes m}$, with $C=H\operatorname{diag}(1,i)H=aI+bX$, to every role, on any number of columns.
children.method: Use additivity of Hamming weight modulo four for orthogonal binary vectors to split each phase change into one-direction phases, conjugate these by the common Hadamard diagonalization into translation kernels, and repair the one nonstandard terminal pair with $C=iZC^{-1}Z$.

motivation.text: All frames are diagonalized by the same $H^{\otimes m}$, so a frame change is a diagonal phase, and an orthonormal residual basis splits it into one two-point kernel per basis vector; the rank budget then counts kernels, each of which will become one smaller layer.

adds.name: phase kernel
adds.meaning: The two-point matrix $C=aI+bX$ with $a=(1+i)/2$ and $b=(1-i)/2$, where $X$ swaps the two coordinates; it satisfies $H_0=b\,\mathsf SC\mathsf S$.

children.salient: The endpoint operator is the same $C^{\otimes m}$ on every role, including scratch roles that held arbitrary values, so the network computes a tensor power of one fixed kernel however its wires are used.

children.claim: For binary $z,w$ with $z\cdot w=0$ the intersection of supports is even, so $\operatorname{wt}(z+w)\equiv\operatorname{wt}(z)+\operatorname{wt}(w)\pmod4$, and if $V=U\perp E$ with orthonormal basis $\mathcal B$ of $E$ then $q_V(x)-q_U(x)=\sum_{v\in\mathcal B}\operatorname{wt}(v)[v\cdot x]\pmod4$, every $\operatorname{wt}(v)$ being odd.

quote.quote: If $z\cdot w=0$, the intersection cardinality is even, so weight is additive modulo four.

children.claim: Each factor $i^{\varepsilon[v\cdot x]}$ with $\varepsilon=\pm1$ equals $\frac{1+i^\varepsilon}{2}+\frac{1-i^\varepsilon}{2}(-1)^{v\cdot x}$, and $H\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)H=X$ on $\operatorname{supp}(v)$ turns $(-1)^{v\cdot x}$ into the translation $X_v$, so each factor becomes $aI+bX_v$ or its inverse and the basis lengths sum to $s_{\rm c}$, with deficit $2N-2L_{\rm c}>0$.

quote.quote: The displayed phase therefore becomes $aI+bX_v$ or its inverse.

children.claim: On $k$ columns $(\mathcal C_V\mathcal C_U^{-1})^{\otimes k}=\prod_{v\in\mathcal B_e}K_{e,v}^{\otimes k}$, so each residual vector contributes one kernel acting on all $k$ columns, $s_{\rm c}$ kernels over the network.

quote.quote: Thus each residual vector contributes one factor acting on all $k$ columns, and there are $s_{\rm c}$ such factors over the network.

children.claim: The zero label has frame $I$ and the full label frame $C^{\otimes m}$; on the route $X_a\to Y_a$ the operator is $C^{-1}$ on the $27$ coordinates of $\operatorname{supp}(u_a)$ and $C$ elsewhere, which $Z_{a,k}$ before and $i^{27k}Z_{a,k}$ after turn into $C^{\otimes mk}$ by $C=iZC^{-1}Z$, and negating the physical $X$ outputs and undoing $\rho$ leaves the forward $C^{\otimes m}$ on every role.

quote.quote: The operator on this pair is therefore $C^{\otimes mk}$ as well.

children.claim: The relative deficits $\eta_{\rm b}=(W_{\rm b}m-s_{\rm b})/(W_{\rm b}m)=339/22587335000000$ and $\eta_{\rm c}=73/19906842167500$ both exceed $20\cdot2^{-50}$, and $\log m<20$ gives $m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-20\cdot2^{-50})>m(1-\eta)$, so $s_{\rm b}/W_{\rm b}<m^\tau$ and $s_{\rm c}/W_{\rm c}<m^\sigma$ with $\tau=\sigma=1-2^{-50}$.

quote.quote: Both exact deficits displayed above are greater than $20\cdot2^{-50}$.

children.claim: One fixed procedure transforms an arbitrary bit array on $[P]\times[2^u]\times[G]\times[2^u]\times[B]$ by $(p,h,g,d,z)\mapsto(p,d,g,h,z)$ in $O(Vu^\tau)$ steps, $V=PGB\,2^{2u}$, including padding and workspace cleanup.
children.method: Prove the bound first for chunks of $e=m^k$ radix-$q$ digits below a row field divisible by $W^k$, by running the bit network on role streams, then supply rows from a few high digits, split the remaining width in base $m$, and pad binary chunk ranges to radix $q$.

motivation.text: Each edge of rational rank $a$ costs $a$ smaller interchanges and the ranks sum to $s<Wm$, so recursing on $1/W$-volume role streams saves a power of the chunk width.

quote.quote: Because the sum of these ranks is less than the number of wires times $m$, the resulting recurrence saves a power of the chunk width.

adds.name: chunk bits
adds.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two interchanged address fields.

adds.name: fixed odd prime
adds.meaning: The fixed odd prime radix in which chunk fields are written, chosen to avoid every denominator of the finite matrix tables.

children.salient: The final effect is an exact permutation of the data, yet the procedure forms pointwise XOR combinations of data in between, and its cost $O(Vu^\tau)$ is below the $\Theta(Vu)$ of moving the $u$ bits one at a time.

children.claim: If fixed circuit data satisfy $M_{\mathrm{out}(\rho(w))}-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}=I_m$ for all $W$ roles and $s=\sum_e\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}A_e<Wm$, and $\tau$ is rational with $s/W<m^\tau$, then two disjoint chunks of $e=m^k$ radix-$q$ digits, below a row field of length divisible by $W^k$, can be interchanged in $O(Ve^\tau)$ time on a fixed number of tapes.
children.method: Write each chunk as $m$ fields of $e/m$ digits, $H$ and $D$, obtain the shear $H\gets H+D$ by running the bit network on $W$ row-split role streams with frames $\Phi_{M_v}$ and recursive edge shears, and interchange by three shears.

motivation.text: The frame identity turns the network's role exchange into one common shear on every row, while each edge shear of rank $a$ costs exactly $a$ recursive interchanges on a stream of $1/W$ of the volume, so the rank budget becomes a recurrence.

adds.name: chunk width
adds.meaning: The number of radix-$q$ digits in each interchanged chunk, $e=m^k$.

adds.name: recursion depth
adds.meaning: The exponent with $e=m^k$, the number of recursion levels.

adds.name: normalized cost
adds.meaning: A uniform bound on running time divided by logical volume for chunks of width $m^k$.

children.salient: Every row, including rows that served as scratch with arbitrary contents, receives exactly the same shear $H\gets H+D$.

children.claim: For a fixed finite set of rational $m\times m$ matrices there is a fixed odd prime $q$ such that each shear $(H,D)\mapsto(H+AD,D)$ over $\mathbb Z/q^b\mathbb Z$ with $\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}A=a$, all $H$ fields lying before all $D$ fields, takes exactly $a$ interchanges of pairs of $b$-digit fields plus $O(V)$ further work.
children.method: Factor $A=E_1\Pi E_2$ with invertible lower triangular $E_1,E_2$ and a partial permutation $\Pi$ with $a$ ones, perform the triangular parts as linear controlled shifts, and realize each one of $\Pi$ with a single interchange.

motivation.text: A controlled shift is linear only when its target follows its controls, which lower triangular coordinate changes respect, so only the rank-$a$ middle factor needs interchanges.

quote.quote: Lower triangular changes of coordinates can be performed entirely in this direction.

children.claim: Every rational $m\times m$ matrix $A$ of rank $a$ factors as $A=E_1\Pi E_2$ with $E_1,E_2$ invertible lower triangular and $\Pi$ a partial permutation matrix with exactly $a$ ones, by eliminating around the rightmost nonzero entry of the topmost nonzero row.

quote.quote: Thus the final partial permutation matrix has exactly $a$ ones.

children.claim: An odd prime $q$ avoiding every denominator and every diagonal numerator in the finite table of factors and inverses makes all these identities hold over $\mathbb Z/q^b\mathbb Z$ with invertible triangular factors.

quote.quote: All these rational identities then specialize to $\mathbb Z/q^b\mathbb Z$, and the triangular factors remain invertible there.

children.claim: A lower triangular transformation of $H$ or of $D$ costs $O(V)$: update coordinates in descending physical order, each by a unit multiple plus a fixed combination of still-original earlier coordinates, using controlled shifts.

quote.quote: A lower triangular transformation of $H$, or of $D$, costs $O(V)$: update coordinates in descending physical order.

children.claim: After transforming $D$ by $E_2$ and $H$ by $E_1^{-1}$, each one of $\Pi$ at $(i,j)$ requires $H_i\gets H_i+D_j$, done as $D_j\gets D_j+H_i$, $(H_i,D_j)\gets(D_j,H_i)$, $D_j\gets H_i-D_j$ with a single interchange, so the number of recursive calls is exactly $a$.

quote.quote: In particular, the number of recursive calls is the rational rank $a$; temporary tapes used for the other operations do not multiply that count.

children.claim: The bit network supplies the required circuit data with $W=W_{\rm b}$ and $s=s_{\rm b}$, its negative source projection already counted in the rank sum.

quote.quote: Proposition~\ref{prop:bit-motif-interface} supplies these conditions with $W=W_{\rm b}$ and $s=s_{\rm b}$.

children.claim: Splitting whole rows cyclically within each prefix, row $Wg+(w-1)$ to role stream $w$, gives $W$ streams with the same shape including the full ranges of $H$ and $D$, each of logical volume $V/W$ and with row count divisible by $W^{k-1}$.

quote.quote: Each has logical volume $V/W$, and its row count is divisible by $W^{k-1}$.

children.claim: Applying $\Phi_{A_e}$ on each edge by the shear procedure, with recursive interchanges of smaller fields, and each gate pointwise, the frame identity gives output $f'_{\rho(w)}=\Phi_{M_{\mathrm{out}(\rho(w))}}\Phi_{-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}}f_w=\Phi_{I_m}f_w$, and merging row $g$ of role $\rho(w)$ back to row $Wg+(w-1)$ yields $H\gets H+D$ on every original row.

quote.quote: The result is $H\leftarrow H+D$ on every original row, including rows assigned to scratch roles, whose initial values were arbitrary.

children.claim: The componentwise updates $D\gets D-H$, $H\gets H+D$, $D\gets H-D$ send $(H,D)$ to $(D,H)$, and only the middle shear uses the circuit.

quote.quote: The transformation sends $(H,D)$ to $(D,H)$.

children.claim: If $F_k$ bounds time divided by logical volume for chunk width $e=m^k$, then $F_0=O(1)$ and $F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)$, hence $F_k=O(e^\tau)$.
children.method: Count a node's recursive calls and their stream volumes, bound the node's own work including fixed-tape scheduling by $O(V)$, divide by $V$, and sum the resulting geometric series.

motivation.text: Dividing by volume makes the $W$ in $s<Wm$ cancel the $1/W$ volume of each call, so one level multiplies the normalized cost by $s/W<m^\tau$ while the width grows by the factor $m$.

children.salient: A node makes $s\approx Wm$ recursive calls, far more than the $m$ subfields its chunk splits into, yet the normalized cost grows by only $s/W<m^\tau$ per level, because each call runs on $1/W$ of the volume.

children.claim: A node makes exactly $s$ recursive calls, one per unit of edge rank, each on one role stream of volume $V/W$ with all other fields as spectators, while its splitting, merging, gates and triangular operations cost $O(V)$.

quote.quote: The number of recursive calls is the sum of the edge ranks, exactly $s$.

children.claim: Hence $F_0=O(1)$ and $F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)$.

quote.quote: F_0=O(1),\qquad F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1).

children.claim: For $s/W<m^\tau$ the sum $\sum_{j\le k}(s/W)^j$ is $O(m^{k\tau})$, at most $k+1$ when $s/W\le1$ and $O((s/W)^k)$ otherwise, so $F_k=O(e^\tau)$.

quote.quote: Hence $F_k=O(e^\tau)$.

children.claim: On fixed tapes, parking the $W-1$ inactive role streams on a stack, copying the active one to the child area and restoring them moves $O(V)$ symbols per child at the parent, and descriptor work is $(\log(2V_0))^{O(1)}=O(V_j)$ because $V_j\ge q^{2e_0}$, so with the fixed number $s$ of children the node overhead stays $O(V)$.

quote.quote: Each push, pop, copy, positioning operation, or erasure moves $O(V)$ symbols at a parent node.

children.claim: Chunks of any $e$ radix-$q$ digits are interchanged in $O(Ve^\tau)$, and chunks of $u$ bits in $O(Vu^\tau)$, by using the top $\rho=\lceil k\log W/(2\log q)\rceil$ digits of both chunks, $k=\lceil\log_me\rceil$, as a padded row field, interchanging base-$m$ pieces of the remaining digits, and padding binary ranges $[2^u]$ to $[q^e]$.
children.method: Supply rows from a few high digits, split the remaining width in base $m$ into power-width pieces sharing one row field, and pad numerically to radix $q$.

motivation.text: The power-width procedure needs a row field divisible by $W^k$; a logarithmic number of the array's own high digits provides one at cost $O(V\log e)$, below $O(Ve^\tau)$.

quote.quote: Rows for a general array can be supplied by a few of its own high digits. Their movement will cost less than the final bound.

children.claim: Interchanging the high digits pair by pair and joining them gives the field order $(d^+,h^+,h^-,g,d^-)$, whose first two fields form a row field of range $R=q^{2\rho}\ge W^k$; zero rows pad it to $R'=W^k\lceil R/W^k\rceil<2R$, so the padded volume stays below $2V$, at cost $O(V\rho)$.

quote.quote: The padded logical volume is less than $2V$.

children.claim: Writing $e-\rho=\sum_{j\le k}a_jm^j$ with $0\le a_j<m$ and interchanging $a_j$ piece pairs of width $m^j$ by the power-width procedure costs $O(V)\sum_ja_jm^{j\tau}=O(Ve^\tau)$, since $a_j<m$ and $m^k<me$.

quote.quote: The fixed bound $a_j<m$ and the inequality $m^k<me$ make this a geometric sum of the stated order.

children.claim: For $u$-bit chunks, padding both ranges from $[2^u]$ to $[q^e]$, with the least $e$ such that $q^e\ge2^u$, grows the volume by less than $q^2$ and preserves entry order, and $e=O(u)$ gives $O(Vu^\tau)$.

quote.quote: Since $e=O(u)$ for fixed $q$, the bound is $O(Vu^\tau)$.

children.claim: Chunks whose widths differ by one bit are interchanged by one single-bit move, costing $O(V)$, plus an equal-width interchange.

quote.quote: Each case uses one single-bit move, costing $O(V)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:elementary-streams}, in addition to the equal-width interchange.

children.claim: For precision $p$, $d=\Theta(p^\epsilon)$, $K=\lfloor d^c\rfloor$ and $r=2^{\Theta(p/d)}$ (later $\epsilon=2^{-75}$ and $c=2^{-56}$), on an array $[P]\times[2^K]^D\times[S]$ with $1\le D\le d$ of polynomial records of $r$ disk-grid coefficients, one fixed procedure returns $Q_p(\mathcal Hz)$, where $\mathcal H=H_0^{\otimes D}$ acts on bit $\rho$ of every chunk, in $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ time, evaluating the layer exactly before one truncation of error below $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$.
children.method: Write $H_0^{\otimes D}$ through the phase kernel as $b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D$, compute $C^{\otimes e}$ by the complex network on row-split role streams with $s_{\rm c}$ children on $e/m$ chunks, implement its binary basis changes by packed selected-bit additions, and bound the exact dyadic growth so all widths stay $O(p)$.

motivation.text: Applying the $D$ butterfly factors one at a time costs $D$ passes, a full factor $d$; grouping them into one tensor power of $C$ lets the complex network's rank saving apply to the number of axes.

quote.quote: We will obtain cost $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$, with $\lambda'<1$ and $V$ the logical bit volume, whereas separate butterfly factors would require $D$ whole-array passes.

adds.name: precision
adds.meaning: The number of fractional bits of the coefficient grid $2^{-p}\mathbb Z[i]$; the multiplier takes $p=6\lceil\log_2n\rceil$.

adds.name: axis bound
adds.meaning: The maximum number of axes or chunks in a layer, $d=\Theta(p^\epsilon)$.

adds.name: chunk width
adds.meaning: The number of address bits $K=\lfloor d^c\rfloor$ in each axis chunk.

adds.name: record length
adds.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in each polynomial record, a power of two $2^{\Theta(p/d)}$.

adds.name: selected chunks
adds.meaning: The number of chunks whose selected bit the layer acts on.

children.claim: On a group of $e=mf$ selected axes divided into $m$ slots of $f$ chunks, each complex-network edge is a fixed binary basis change of the columns around one forward child $C^{\otimes f}$ on one slot per residual vector, so the network yields $C^{\otimes e}$ on every role from exactly $s_{\rm c}$ children, and $H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D$ converts the result into the normalized layer.
children.method: Conjugate translation kernels into coordinate directions by an invertible binary matrix, write that matrix as a fixed number of row additions, and turn inverse children into forward ones by sign and phase wrappers.

motivation.text: Residual basis vectors are arbitrary binary directions; moving them onto coordinate slots by an invertible binary matrix lets each kernel act on whole consecutive chunks, which is a smaller instance of the same layer.

quote.quote: The next step puts those directions into coordinate positions without performing a general transpose.

children.claim: $C=H\mathsf SH$ with $\mathsf S=\operatorname{diag}(1,i)$ satisfies $H_0=b\mathsf SC\mathsf S$, $C^2=X$, $C^4=I$ and $C^{-1}=bI+aX=-iZCZ$, all with Gaussian dyadic coefficients.

quote.quote: These identities use only Gaussian dyadic coefficients.

children.claim: Since $\mathcal P_MX_v\mathcal P_M^{-1}=X_{Mv}$, taking an orthonormal residual basis as the first columns of an invertible binary $M$ gives $\mathcal C_{U_+}\mathcal C_{U_-}^{-1}=\mathcal P_M(\prod_jC_{e_j}^{\epsilon_j})\mathcal P_M^{-1}$, using only the invertibility of $M$.

quote.quote: The matrix $M$ need not preserve the dot product: equation~\eqref{eq:phase-conjugation} only uses its invertibility.

children.claim: With columns $(x_{1,j},\dots,x_{m,j})$ for $0\le j<f$, the edge is $\mathcal P_M^{-1}$ on every column, then $(C^{\epsilon_h})^{\otimes f}$ on slot $h$ for each residual vector, then $\mathcal P_M$, and $(C^{-1})^{\otimes f}=(-i)^fZ^{\otimes f}C^{\otimes f}Z^{\otimes f}$ makes every child a forward call.

quote.quote: A negative directional kernel still requires only one forward child, because

children.claim: Any $M\in\operatorname{GL}(m,\mathbb F_2)$ is a product of at most $m(m-1)+3m$ row additions, and adding row $h'$ to row $h$ in every column XORs the corresponding selected bits of two whole slots.

quote.quote: Thus one row addition changes corresponding selected positions in two whole slots.

children.claim: Running the network with these column frames on $e=mf$ selected axes makes exactly $s_{\rm c}$ child calls, each on the $f=e/m$ axes of one slot, and gives $C^{\otimes e}$ on every role, besides a fixed number of row additions and coefficientwise scalar operations.

quote.quote: Summing its residual dimensions gives exactly $s_{\rm c}$ child calls, each on the $f=e/m$ axes of one slot.

children.claim: With $(\mathcal S_Dz)(x)=i^{x_1+\cdots+x_D}z(x)$, $H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D$, and $b^D=(-i/2)^{\lfloor D/2\rfloor}b^{D\bmod2}$ is a binary shift and a fourth-root phase, so the whole layer is exact up to its final truncation.

quote.quote: Thus, once the physical binary basis changes and recursive stream layout are supplied, the complete parallel butterfly layer is exact up to its prescribed final truncation.

children.claim: On $R$-bit records over $[N_0]\times[2^L]_{\chi_1}\times[N_1]\times[2^L]_{\chi_2}\times[N_2]\times[2^L]_{\chi_3}\times[N_3]$ with $L=fK$ and $K\ge6$, one procedure performs $y_{j_i}\gets y_{j_i}\oplus x_{j_i}$ at $j_i=\rho+iK$ for $0\le i<f$, restoring chunk $z$ and every payload, in time $O(V(L^\tau+1)+MA_{\rm rect}^3+\delta_{\rm bad}MA_{\rm rect}(R+A_{\rm rect}))$ with $\delta_{\rm bad}=\min\{1,80(f-1)2^{-K}\}$, which is $O(V(L^\tau+1))$ when $A_{\rm rect}=O(p)$, $R$ exceeds every fixed power of $p$ and $K/\log p\to\infty$.
children.method: Flip the parities of $K$-bit segments by eight packed conditional additions, each one cyclic shift of a whole chunk with a target-independent offset, which agree with the ideal XOR map except on addresses with extreme guard values; then move exactly those exceptional records into place by sorting.

motivation.text: Parity flips can be built from additions of $\pm1$, and adding to all $f$ segments at once is a single controlled cyclic shift of the whole chunk as long as no segment carries; guard values make carries rare, and the rare exceptional addresses form a small stream that sorting repairs deterministically.

adds.name: selected positions
adds.meaning: The number of selected bit positions $j_i=\rho+iK$ in each chunk of $L=fK$ bits.

adds.name: bad addresses
adds.meaning: The set of addresses at which some guard value lies within ten of an end of its range, where the packed shifts may carry between segments.

children.salient: The procedure is deterministic and worst-case although its fast part is wrong on some addresses: the exceptional set depends only on addresses, has fraction at most $80(f-1)2^{-K}$, and is repaired exactly.

children.claim: For a control $c$ and integers $u,w$, the eight conditional updates of $u$ and $w$ by $\pm c$, tested on the parity of the other, induce the cycle $(00\ 01\ 10)$ and then $(01\ 10\ 11)$ on parity pairs, composing to $(00\ 10)(01\ 11)$, so $(u',w')=(u+c(1-2(u\bmod2)),w)$ and each coordinate moves by at most four.

quote.quote: Thus the parity of $u$ is flipped precisely when $c=1$, both quotients under division by two are preserved, and the arbitrary auxiliary integer $w$ is restored.

children.claim: Omitting the top position $j_{f-1}$, one line applied to all $K$-bit segments at once is the single cyclic shift $y\gets y+\varepsilon\sum_{i=0}^{f-2}2^{j_i}[x_{j_i}=1][z_{j_i}=b]\pmod{2^L}$ (or with $y,z$ exchanged), a bijection because its offset never depends on its target; $S_0$ denotes the composition of the eight lines.

quote.quote: The shift offset never depends on its target chunk, so each line is a bijection of the rectangle.

children.claim: Outside the set $\mathcal B$ of addresses where some guard value $g$ of $y$ or $z$ violates $10\le g\le2^{K-1}-11$, every segment stays inside $[0,2^K-1]$ under displacement eight, so no segment carries or borrows and $S_0$ agrees with the ideal map $T_0$ that performs the XORs.

quote.quote: Inductively, each packed addition therefore agrees with all the independent segment additions: no segment carries into or borrows from the next segment.

children.claim: Each guard excludes twenty of its $2^{K-1}$ values, so the union bound over the $2(f-1)$ guards gives $|\mathcal B|\le\delta_{\rm bad}M$, independently of the record values.

quote.quote: No record value enters this count.

children.claim: $T_0$ preserves guard values and hence $\mathcal B$, and $S_0,T_0$ are bijections that agree off $\mathcal B$, so $T_0S_0^{-1}$ fixes $\mathcal B^c$ and permutes $\mathcal B$.

quote.quote: Thus $T_0S_0^{-1}$ fixes $\mathcal B^c$ and permutes $\mathcal B$.

children.claim: Each rotation is a chunk interchange moving its target after its two controls, costing $O(VL^\tau)$, an $O(V)$ controlled shift whose offset is computed from the controls in $L^{O(1)}$ time, and the interchange undone, with at most sixteen interchanges and eight rotations in all.

quote.quote: There are at most sixteen swaps and eight rotations in $S_0$.

children.claim: Scanning with a rank counter, the records in $\mathcal B$ are extracted with destination ranks $\operatorname{rank}(q')=\operatorname{rank}(q)+\sum_h(q'_h-q_h)\sigma_h$ for $q'=T_0(S_0^{-1}(q))$, stably radix-sorted, and reinserted into the marked holes, which implements $T_0$ on every address.

quote.quote: This implements $T_0$ everywhere.

children.claim: A final two-bit XOR on $x_{j_{f-1}},y_{j_{f-1}}$ costs $O(V)$ and supplies the omitted position; when $f=1$ it is the whole algorithm.

quote.quote: When $f=1$, $S_0,T_0$ are identities, $\mathcal B$ is empty, and this last step is the entire algorithm.

children.claim: Movement costs $O(V(L^\tau+1))$, record scans $O(MA_{\rm rect}^3+V)$ and radix passes $O(|\mathcal B|A_{\rm rect}(R+A_{\rm rect}))$; divided by $V=MR$ the extra terms are $A_{\rm rect}^3/R\to0$ and $O(p^22^{-K}(1+A_{\rm rect}/R))=o(1)$.

quote.quote: Under the stated family bounds the first tends to zero, and the second is $O(p^2 2^{-K}(1+A_{\rm rect}/R))=o(1)$.

children.claim: A fixed binary change of basis on $e=mf$ axes is a fixed number of such row additions, using slot $h'$ as $x$, slot $h$ as $y$ and any third slot as $z$, so it and its inverse cost $O(V((eK)^\tau+1))$.

quote.quote: the complete change of basis and its inverse therefore cost $O(V((eK)^\tau+1))$ on a stream of volume $V$.

children.claim: With the first $q_0=\lceil\log_2W\rceil\lceil\log_m(2d)\rceil$ chunks used as rows and the remaining $D-q_0$ chunks split into base-$m$ pieces, the complex network computes $C^{\otimes D}$ in $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$, from $F(e)\le(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^\tau+1)$ and $F(e)=O(e)$ for $e<d^\beta$, with $\beta=1/2$, $\lambda=1-2^{-52}$ and $\lambda'=1-2^{-54}$.
children.method: Supply rows from the first chunks, split rows into the $W$ roles at every node so each child has $1/W$ of the volume, and unroll the volume-normalized recurrence into internal-node and leaf contributions.

motivation.text: As for interchanges, normalizing by volume turns $s$ children on $1/W$ of the volume into the factor $s/W<m^\sigma$, so recursion on the number of axes saves a power once the node overhead $(eK)^\tau$ is controlled by $K\le d^c$.

children.claim: One kernel $C(u,v)=((u+v+i(u-v))/2,(u+v-i(u-v))/2)$ on a selected bit is a split on that bit, an exact paired coefficient scan and a merge, costing $O(V)$, so $e$ individual kernels cost $O(Ve)$.

quote.quote: Thus \(e\) individual kernels cost \(O(Ve)\) on any stream with these complete ranges and record format.

children.claim: An internal node with $e=m^k$ chunks makes exactly $s$ recursive calls on slots of $e/m$ chunks, and its basis changes, scalar gates, endpoint corrections and reassembly cost $O(V((eK)^\tau+1))$.

quote.quote: The phase construction supplies one recursive call on a slot for each vector in an edge residual basis, hence exactly \(s\) calls in one invocation of the network.

children.claim: If $D\le q_0$, individual kernels cost $O(V\log d)$; otherwise $C$ is applied individually on the first $q_0$ chunks, whose bits then form a row index of range $2^{q_0K}\ge W^{k_0}$ with $k_0=\lceil\log_md\rceil$, padded with zero rows to a multiple of $W^{k_0}$, at most doubling the volume.

quote.quote: If \(D\le q_0\), use individual \(C\) kernels, at cost \(O(V\log d)\).

children.claim: Sending row $Wg+w$ to role $w$ gives role streams with the same remaining shape, existing rows serving as scratch, so every recursive edge call acts on exactly $1/W$ of its parent's logical volume.

quote.quote: Each recursive edge call acts on one role stream with volume exactly \(1/W\) of its parent's logical volume.

children.claim: Hence the time per unit volume satisfies $F(e)\le(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^\tau+1)$ for $e\ge d^\beta$, and $F(e)=O(e)$ below.

quote.quote: Dividing by the current volume \(V\) gives the factor \(s/W\).

children.claim: At internal nodes $K\le d^c\le e^{c/\beta}$, so the overhead is $O(e^{\tau(1+c/\beta)}+1)=O(e^\lambda)$ and the internal costs sum to $O(e^\lambda)$ because $s/W\le m^\sigma<m^\lambda$, while leaves after $j$ levels with $e/m^j<d^\beta$ chunks contribute $O(e^\sigma d^{\beta(1-\sigma)})$.

quote.quote: The overhead is therefore \(O(e^{\tau(1+c/\beta)}+1)=O(e^\lambda)\).

children.claim: Over the at most $(m-1)(1+\lfloor\log_md\rfloor)$ base-$m$ pieces of the remaining $D-q_0$ chunks, plus the row preprocessing, the total is $O(\log(2d)[d^\lambda+d^{\sigma+\beta(1-\sigma)}+1])=O(d^{\lambda'})$ for any fixed $\max\{\lambda,\sigma+\beta(1-\sigma)\}<\lambda'<1$.

quote.quote: There are at most \((m-1)(1+\lfloor\log_m d\rfloor)\) pieces.

children.claim: Within one layer every intermediate coefficient has arithmetic depth at most $\Delta=\lceil C_0d^{C_1}\rceil$, with $C_1=20$, $C_0=128mB^2$, $B=s+E$ and $E=64(W+m+1)^3$, so $p+\Delta$ fractional and $\Delta+3$ integer bits represent every value exactly, and $\Delta=o(p)$ because $\epsilon C_1<1$.
children.method: Bound the dependency depth by the recurrence $A(e)\le sA(e/m)+E$ with leaves $8e$, add the outer corrections, and convert depth into denominator and magnitude growth.

motivation.text: Intermediate network operators can enlarge values, so exact evaluation needs explicit guard bits, and the depth of the computation bounds both denominator and magnitude growth.

quote.quote: Its intermediate operators need not be contractions.

adds.name: guard width
adds.meaning: The number of extra fractional bits, and of integer bits less three, reserved per real component during one layer.

children.claim: For the $h=100$ complex network $m^{10}<B<m^{11}$, so $\nu=\min\{j:m^j\ge B\}=11$ and $C_1=\max\{20,\nu+3\}=20$.

quote.quote: These values give \(m^{10}<B<m^{11}\), hence \(\nu=11\) and \(C_1=20\).

children.claim: Each wire meets at most twelve scalar gates of at most $W$ inputs with coefficients in $\{0,\pm1,\pm1/2\}$, so the gates take at most $24W^3$ operations, the child corrections $4s$ and the endpoint corrections $4W+4$, in total below $E=64(W+m+1)^3$ since $s<Wm$.

quote.quote: Since \(s<Wm\), the total \(24W^3+4s+4W+4\) is less than \(E=64(W+m+1)^3\).

children.claim: Concatenating the $s$ child calls, the depth satisfies $A(e)\le sA(e/m)+E$ at internal nodes and $A(e)\le8e$ at leaves.

quote.quote: The depth estimate concatenates the \(s\) calls, so it uses \(s\).
Starting with \(8e\le8d\le8dB\) at a leaf and applying this inequality through the levels gives the first bound below.

children.claim: By induction a value at arithmetic depth $\ell$ lies in $2^{-(p+\ell)}\mathbb Z[i]$ with modulus at most $2^\ell$, so $p+\Delta$ fractional and $\Delta+3$ integer and sign bits per component suffice with no rounding and no overflow.

quote.quote: Thus reserving \(p+\Delta\) fractional bits and \(\Delta+3\) integer and sign bits per real component represents every intermediate coefficient exactly and prevents overflow.

children.claim: Choosing $\epsilon C_1<1$ with $d=\Theta(p^\epsilon)$ makes $\Delta=o(p)$, so the guarded coefficient width is $O(p)$ as the time analysis requires.

quote.quote: Since \(d=\Theta(p^\epsilon)\), \(\Delta=o(p)\), and the full coefficient width is \(O(p)\), as required in the time analysis.

children.claim: Uniformly for $p\ge p_0$ in the bands $a_dp^\epsilon\le d\le b_dp^\epsilon$ and $2^{a_rp/d}\le r\le2^{b_rp/d}$, every packed call has width parameter $A_*\le C_Ap$, $K\ge6$, $K/\log p\to\infty$ and superpolynomial records, so it costs $O(M_{\rm child}R_{\rm g}(L^\tau+1))$, and the whole layer costs $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ on fixed tapes.

quote.quote: The row construction and the recurrence analysis above give total time $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ on fixed tapes, including all padded and auxiliary streams.

children.claim: Every row of $\mathcal H$ has absolute row sum one, so $\mathcal H$ maps disk arrays to disk arrays, and truncating each component toward zero once keeps the disk with error below $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$.

quote.quote: Finally, every row of $\mathcal H$ has absolute row sum one.
